I'll verify the runtime capabilities (AI entry points, tools, available events) so the persona catalogue is grounded in what the engine can actually do.Let me confirm the AI/SmolAgent entry points and the full tool registry, since persona feasibility depends on them.# Persona Catalogue & Other Ways to Let AI Manage the Project ## 1. How to reason about "which cases" A persona is not a job title — it is a **contract with five parts**. Every candidate case is only worth building if you can answer these five: | Question | What it decides | Failure if unanswered | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Oracle** — what tells us "this is wrong"? | The real decision model (test suite, scanner, health check, diff, metric) | The LLM invents a verdict → noise + cost | | **Scope** — what may it read? | Board/column/tag/date window + file paths | Context bloat, cost, prompt injection surface | | **Trigger** — when does it run? | `interval` / `event` / `manual` | Either burns money or never fires | | **Write authority** — what may it change? | `observe` → `suggest` → `apply` → `act` | Two personas fighting over one field | | **Budget** — who pays? | `persona.user` wallet + `Chat.estimation_cost` | Silent cost runaway | > **Key insight:** the best personas wrap an **external oracle**, not a model. The LLM's job is *translation, triage and prioritisation* — never judgement. A test suite, `docker_ps`, a CVE feed or a lint run is a far better "decision model" than Laya or any LLM, and it costs nothing. Laya/LLMs earn their keep only for the ambiguous 20% (is this task actually the same as that one? does this log line matter?). The codebase already gives us most oracles (verified in `codx/junior/`): | Oracle | Already exists | | :--- | :--- | | Test verdict | `CODXJuniorSession.project_script_test()` → `None` (no script) / `""` (pass) / stdout (fail, matched by `settings.script_test_check_regex`) | | Patch application | `session.apply_patch(patch)`, `apply_file_changes` tool | | Container health | `docker_ps`, `docker_logs`, `docker_stats`, `docker_inspect`, `docker_compose_service` | | Repo state | `get_file_last_version`, `project_structure`, `project_search` (glob + semantic) | | Web/UI behaviour | `start_session`, `browse_action`, `get_screenshot`, `get_source_code` | | Knowledge/doc drift | `WikiManager.build_dependency_graph / build_domains / build_wiki_index`, `KnowledgeAISearch.ai_search` | | Task history | `Chat.status_history` (append-only transitions), `Chat.cost` | | External issues | `GitIssuesAgent` (downloads issue + comments → reasoning → subtasks) | | Arbitrary scripted check | `ProjectScript` model + `exec_command` / `/api/run/script` | ⚠️ **Constraint to remember:** `create_task` and `process_task` tools require `settings._active_session` and `settings._current_chat` — they only work when the persona runs **inside a chat context** (SmolAgent run). Standalone handlers must use `ChatManager` directly. This shapes the design: *personas should act through a chat, not beside it.* --- ## 2. The catalogue | Persona | Oracle (the real judge) | Trigger | Writes | Cost | Risk | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Tony — Project Manager** | task invariants (overdue, progress≠status, stale) | interval 30m | `status`, `priority`, `progress`, `due_date` | none (rule-based) | low | | **Quinn — QA / Test** | `project_script_test`, browser tools | event `task.done`, interval 1h | `status`→`rejected`/`done`, new defect tasks, `progress` | low-medium | medium | | **Sentinel — CISO / Security** | scanners as `ProjectScript` (pip-audit, npm audit, semgrep), CVE lookup via `fetch_webpage` | interval daily, event `release.ready` | `priority`, `tags`, new tasks, **never code** | low | medium | | **Ops — DevOps / SRE** | `docker_*`, logs, `ProjectScript.status`, health endpoints | event `deploy.*`, interval 5m | incidents/tasks, container lifecycle (gated) | low | **high** | | **Ada — Tech Lead / Architect** | `project_structure`, dependency graph, wiki | interval weekly, event `pr.ready` | `tags`, new refactor tasks, review comments | medium | low | | **Rita — Release Manager** | git state + green tests + checklist | manual, event `sprint.end` | `sprints`, release notes, board moves | low | medium | | **Dora — Documentation** | `WikiManager` drift vs `get_file_last_version` | event `file.changed`, interval daily | docs files, wiki, `description` | medium | low | | **Max — Triage / Intake** | `duckduckgo_search`, `project_search`, issue text | event `task.created` | `board/column`, `assignees`, `priority`, `tags` | medium | low | | **Penny — FinOps** | `Chat.cost`, `estimation_cost`, raw AI logs | interval daily | budgets, `priority` for expensive tasks | none | low | | **Dependabot-like — Upgrades** | registry versions, changelog fetch | interval weekly | **PR/patch only** + tasks | medium | medium | | **Schema — DB / Migrations** | migration files, git history | event `file.changed` on migrations | new review tasks, `priority` | low | medium | | **Atlas — Accessibility / i18n** | browser tools + missing keys scan | interval weekly | new tasks, `tags` | medium | low | --- ## 3. Deep dives on your three candidates ### 3.1 QA / Testing — **the strongest persona to build second** **Why it works:** QA has the only *objective* pass/fail oracle in the system. That makes it self-verifying: no human needs to trust the persona, they trust the test run. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[event: task.done
or interval] --> B[load tasks in 'doing'/'review'] B --> C[session.project_script_test] C -->|None| D[skip: no script_test] C -->|empty| E[verdict PASS] C -->|stdout| F[verdict FAIL] E --> G[progress=100, status=done] F --> H[status=rejected
create defect task with stdout] ``` **Design:** - **Two handlers**, not one: `run_tests` (deterministic, no LLM) and `triage_failures` (LLM, maps stdout → defect task title/description). - **Defect tasks** are created in a dedicated board/column (`qa/defects`) with `parent_id` = original task, `priority` = `high`, and the raw log attached as the first message — so a human/agent can reproduce. - **Never auto-`done` a task whose `project_script_test` returned `None`** (no script configured). That's the #1 false-positive source. - Add **UI/regression mode** behind a second, manual trigger using the browser tools (`start_session` → `browse_action` → `get_screenshot`); this is the expensive path, keep it manual. ```json { "name": "quinn", "profile": "qa_engineer", "enabled": true, "triggers": [ { "type": "event", "event": "task.status_changed", "task": "run_tests", "prompt": "Task {{chat_name}} moved to {{to_status}}. Verify it." }, { "type": "interval", "interval_minutes": 60, "task": "run_tests" } ] } ``` **Guardrails:** `allowed_tools: [project_read_file, project_search, create_task, apply_file_changes]` — explicitly **no** `project_write_file`, no docker. --- ### 3.2 CISO / Security — **advisory-only, and always will be** **Why it's valuable:** security drift is continuous and cheap to detect, expensive to miss. **Why it must be weak:** a persona with write access to code + infra is a liability with no accountability chain. **Design — capability ladder capped at L2:** - **L0/observe:** run `pip-audit` / `npm audit` / `semgrep` as a `ProjectScript`, parse results. - **L1/suggest:** open a *security board* with one task per finding: `priority` from CVSS, `due_date` from severity policy, `tags: [security, cve-XXXX]`, `assignees: []` (human must claim). - **L2/apply (only these writes, allowed):** `priority`, `tags`, `status` on other tasks (e.g. block a release task), and `estimation_cost` warnings. - **Never:** `project_write_file`, dependency version bumps, `apply_patch`. **Note:** there is no built-in security scanner in the repo. The oracle must be a script — either `ProjectScript` entries or a `script_test`-style command. This is a *feature*: it makes the CISO's authority auditable ("findings come from `semgrep --json`"), which is exactly what a security review needs. ```json { "name": "sentinel", "profile": "ciso", "triggers": [ { "type": "interval", "interval_minutes": 1440, "task": "security_audit" }, { "type": "event", "event": "release.requested", "task": "security_gate" } ] } ``` `security_gate` returns a **verdict object**, not mutations: `{ "block": true, "findings": [...], "reason": "3 high CVEs in deps" }` — the release persona reads it. This is the **"veto, don't write"** pattern, and it generalises to any compliance role (privacy, licensing). --- ### 3.3 DevOps / SRE — **highest value, highest blast radius → hardest gating** **Why it's valuable:** this is where the operations knowledge already lives (`docker_*` tools, `ProjectScript` lifecycle, log reading). An SRE persona that *explains* a crash loop in plain language is worth a lot. **Design — split into three personas with different write authority** (a common trap is one omnipotent "DevOps" persona): | Sub-persona | Authority | May write | May NOT | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Ops-Watch** (always on, cheap) | L1 | incident tasks, `priority`, notifications | anything touching containers | | **Ops-Diagnose** (event-driven) | L1 | root-cause summary on incidents, `tags` | container lifecycle | | **Ops-Remediate** (manual/gated) | L3 | `docker_restart`, `docker_compose_start`, `docker_logs` retention | `docker_run`, image pulls, compose file edits | **Why the split matters:** diagnosing (read-only, LLM-heavy, safe) and remediating (write, dangerous, deterministic) have completely different cost and risk profiles. Remediation should be **rule-based, not LLM-based**: "if container X exited non-zero → restart it, max 2 times per hour, then escalate." The LLM only writes the post-mortem. **Incident loop:** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as Ops-Watch participant EM as EventManager / background participant T as Task board (incidents) participant H as Human W->>EM: poll docker_ps + docker_logs (5 min) EM-->>W: container unhealthy W->>T: create_task(incident, logs attached, assignees=[]) W->>H: send_notification(socket) Note over H: Human (or Ops-Remediate) acts ``` **Guardrails:** `allowed_tools` must exclude `docker_run`, `docker_compose_run` (arbitrary image execution = remote code execution path); `estimation_cost` mandatory; per-container cooldown so a crash-looping container doesn't trigger an infinite persona loop. --- ### 3.4 The rest, in one line each - **Tech Lead / Architect** — weekly: read `project_structure` + dependency graph + `status_history`; output = *structural* tasks (split god-files, break cycles). Oracle = coupling/ownership metrics, not opinion. - **Release Manager** — manual trigger only. Compiles a release note from merged tasks; moves `done` tasks to `released`; blocks if CISO said `block: true`. - **Documentation (Dora)** — the only persona allowed to write docs files. Oracle = wiki drift (file changed since last wiki build). Very high value/cost ratio, near-zero risk. - **Triage (Max)** — on `task.created`: enrich `tags`, set `priority`, route to board/column, propose `assignees` from past ownership (`status_history.user`). The **highest-fanout, lowest-risk** persona. - **FinOps (Penny)** — reads `Chat.cost` + raw AI logs; flags tasks whose spend will exceed `estimation_cost`; **pure rules, zero LLM**. - **Dependency Updater** — the only persona allowed to produce patches unattended, and only as **PRs judged by CI**. Never merges. - **Schema / Migrations** — reviews migration tasks for destructive operations (`DROP`, `NOT NULL` without default) → raises `priority` and adds a checklist. Rule + LLM hybrid. - **Accessibility / i18n** — browser tools + key scans; produces tasks only. --- ## 4. Field ownership — the design detail that prevents chaos If two personas write `status`, you get an oscillation that looks like a bug and burns money. **Assign one owner per field, everyone else reads.** | Field | Owner persona | Everyone else | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `status` (`todo`/`doing`) | Tony (PM) | QA may set `rejected`/`done` after a verdict | | `status` (`rejected`/`done`) | Quinn (QA) | Tony reads | | `priority` | Tony; Sentinel may escalate to `high` | others read | | `progress` | Tony (derived from status) | nobody | | `due_date` | **humans only** | nobody (see below) | | `assignees` | **humans only** (except Max proposing) | nobody | | `tags` | Max + Sentinel | others read | | `board`/`column` | Max (triage) | others read | | `estimation_cost` | Penny proposes, humans decide | nobody | | repo files | Dora (docs), Dependabot (via PR) | nobody | **Anti-patterns to refuse:** - ❌ **Auto-merger persona** — code personas must stop at "PR + CI verdict". - ❌ **Persona that assigns itself work** — creates an unbounded self-triggering loop. - ❌ **Persona that invents `due_date`** — dates are commitments owed by humans. - ❌ **"AI manager" that renames/retags everything** — high churn, no signal; measure churn per run and kill it. - ❌ **Two personas with the same trigger + same writes** — they will duel at 3am. --- ## 5. Other ways to have the project managed by AI Beyond "interval persona reviews the board", there are at least ten distinct architectures. They compose: ### A. Board-as-state-machine (column triggers) — *pull model* Columns are states; a persona subscribes to a column, not to a timer. `event: columN.entered("Review")` → reviewer persona. **Why:** management becomes visible and controllable — moving a card *is* the command. Humans get an undo button (drag it back). This is the single best UX for AI management. ### B. Work-queue drainer (agent workforce) Persona claims a task (`assignees += persona`), locks it, runs `process_task(chat_id, wait=False)`, then releases. This is what `create_task` + `process_task` tools were built for. **Why:** throughput is bounded by WIP limits, not by cron. Add a `claim` lock to prevent two personas grabbing the same card. ### C. Pipeline with gates (intake → plan → implement → verify → release) Each stage = one persona + one **gate**. Gates are `decision` objects (`apply` vs `propose` vs `block`), not free text. **Why:** it turns autonomy into a *dial per stage* — you can have a fully autonomous planner and a human-gated releaser. ### D. Supervisor / meta-persona (Tony 2.0) Tony stops editing tasks and starts **dispatching**: it reads the board, decides *which* persona should handle what, and creates tasks assigned to personas (`assignees: ["quinn"]`) — a `persona`-aware assignee, since personas are users. **Why:** personas shouldn't each scan the whole board; one coordinator with a global view is cheaper and avoids duplicated work. Risk: single point of failure → keep it rule-based, cap dispatches per hour. ### E. Rituals (cron with a name) Same interval trigger, different prompts and cadence: | Ritual | Cadence | Output | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Daily standup digest | 24h | message in a `standups` board: what moved, what's stuck | | Weekly planning | 7d | proposed `priority`/`due_date` *suggestions* | | Monthly audit | 30d | stale tasks → archive proposal, debt tasks | | Quarterly arch review | 90d | structural tasks + wiki refresh | **Why:** rituals are what humans actually recognise as "management", and they're naturally the lowest-risk (output = text, not mutations). ### F. Zero-LLM watchdogs (invariants) Pure `RuleBasedDecisionModel` on cheap fields: WIP limits, budget breaches, stale-in-`doing`, orphaned tasks, tasks with no `estimator_cost`. **Why:** 80% of "management" is bookkeeping. Paying tokens for arithmetic is waste, and rules are auditable. ### G. Advisory personas (suggest, never write) Instead of `update_chat_metadata`, write a **proposal chat**: `mode: "task"`, `parent_id` = target task, first message = structured proposal + JSON diff of proposed fields, `assignees: []`. **Why:** this is the correct **L1** for every risky persona. It gives you an audit trail, an approval queue, and — critically — a labelled dataset of accepted/rejected proposals to evaluate the persona. ### H. CI as judge, AI as author For anything touching code: persona → patch/PR → existing CI decides → human merges. **Why:** it's the only pattern where the AI's quality is measured by machinery instead of opinion. `session.apply_patch` + `project_script_test` already implement the loop. ### I. External-system mirroring (auditability) Mirror the AI's work into GitHub issues/PRs (`GitIssuesAgent` is the seed) so every AI action has an author identity and appears in a system your auditors already trust. **Why:** "what did the AI do last week?" is answerable in git history, not in a JSONL log. ### J. Self-measuring loop (personas as hypotheses) `Chat.status_history` is an append-only transition log — that is a ready-made evaluation dataset. Track per persona: - **precision** — % of its mutations a human didn't immediately revert - **cost per accepted decision** - **override rate** — humans undoing its writes - **time-to-signal** — how long errors survive before it catches them **Why:** without this, personas accrete forever and nobody can justify or kill one. With it, "disable Penny" becomes a data decision. Recommend a `persona_run` record (persona, trigger, decisions, applied, cost, duration) from day one. ### K. Conversational management Manual trigger + `@tony` mention inside a task chat: "replan this sprint", "why is this stuck?". **Why:** the cheapest way to get value on day one, and it produces the prompts that later become automated triggers. `MentionManager` already parses `@codx:` markers in source files — the same idea for task comments. ### L. Paired personas (author + reviewer) Never one persona with both `project_write_file` and the verdict. Dora writes docs / Ada reviews them. Dependabot patches / QA runs tests. **Why:** separates generation from judgement — the structural reason human teams have code review at all. --- ## 6. Capability ladder (rollout order) ```mermaid flowchart LR L0[L0 Observe
digests, no writes] --> L1[L1 Suggest
proposal chats] L1 --> L2[L2 Apply
